cv_derivation: equal_width scenario applies TIER1_HALF_WIDTH=0.25 (a uniform prior of baseline*[1-0.25, 1+0.25] = baseline*[0.75, 1.25]) to ALL 14 parameters regardless of evidence tier (sobol_driver_v2.py make_bounds(), branch `elif scenario == 'equal_width': hw = TIER1_HALF_WIDTH`). For a Uniform(a,b) distribution centered on the baseline with half-width hw (a=base*(1-hw), b=base*(1+hw)), std = hw*base/sqrt(3), so CV = std/mean = hw/sqrt(3) = 0.25/sqrt(3) = 0.144338 (~0.144). This 'CV ~ 0.144, half-width 25%' figure is stated verbatim, for the same TIER1_HALF_WIDTH, in sobol_driver.py's own header comment (line 20) -- i.e. the project's own code already reports this exact CV for this exact half-width, confirming the derivation rather than introducing a new one.
selection_rationale: TIER1_HALF_WIDTH=0.25 (and hence CV~0.144) was NOT independently chosen for the equal_width scenario -- it reuses, unchanged, the SAME half-width already used for 'Tier 1' (well-supported) parameters in the as_documented scenario (sobol_driver_v2.py / sobol_driver.py: as_documented gives Tier-2 params the wider TIER2_HALF_WIDTH=0.60 and Tier-1 params TIER1_HALF_WIDTH=0.25). The equal_width scenario's explicit purpose (per sobol_driver.py's module docstring and ml/robustness_audit.py's PriorSpec/make_bounds docstring) is a robustness stress test: apply the SAME (narrow, Tier-1) half-width to every parameter -- including the ones normally given the wider Tier-2 width -- to check whether k_T4_entry's apparent dominance in the as_documented Sobol ranking is a real mechanistic effect or simply an artifact of giving it (and 4 other Tier-2 params: t4_dose_total, inf_threshold, rho_g, rho_i) a wider prior than everyone else. IMPORTANT -- what the code does NOT show: there is no evidence in the code/comments that TIER1_HALF_WIDTH=0.25 itself was matched to any specific Tier-1 parameter's independently documented/literature CV. sobol_driver.py's own header states plainly that no prior-width spec file was recoverable from the original repo and that both TIER1_HALF_WIDTH=0.25 and TIER2_HALF_WIDTH=0.60 are 'ASSUMPTIONS FLAGGED EXPLICITLY ... constructed here, not recovered from Kartheek's original calibration.' So the honest rule is: 'equal_width = give every parameter the already-defined Tier-1 half-width', not 'equal_width = matched to parameter X's documented CV'.
